Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test constructs a 3x2 BigMatrix and multiplies it by a 2-element vector:
- Matrix a has 3 rows and 2 columns.
- Vector v has length 2, which matches the matrix’s column dimension, so the dimension check should pass.

Inspecting BigMatrixImpl.operate(BigDecimal[]) shows:
- It correctly validates v.length == getColumnDimension() (lines 986–988).
- It determines the number of rows and columns (lines 989–990).
- It incorrectly allocates the result vector with the length of the input vector: new BigDecimal[v.length] (line 991).
- It then iterates over all rows (0 to nRows - 1) and writes to out[row] (lines 992–997).

For a non-square matrix (3x2 in the test), this causes an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when row reaches 2 because out has length 2 but is indexed with 2. This aligns exactly with the current bug report’s description: the result vector is wrongly sized to the input vector length instead of the matrix’s row dimension, which leads to runtime exceptions for non-square matrices and incorrect results.

Correct behavior: The result vector length must be equal to the matrix row dimension. The fix is to allocate out as new BigDecimal[nRows] instead of new BigDecimal[v.length]. This issue mirrors the reported problem for RealMatrixImpl and is present here in BigMatrixImpl as well.
